A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same VidComposition research work. All 17 pages in each version, including Supplementary Sections 7–11, support comparison; text extraction and rendered-page checks reveal no material gaps.

before.justification: v4 reports original model and human evaluation results on VidComposition in Table 2, along with diagnostic experiments and qualitative analyses in the main text and supplement.

after.justification: v5 retains these original benchmark results, diagnostic experiments, and qualitative analyses, including the supplementary results.

M1.justification: The benchmark construction and prediction procedure are identical, including Algorithm 1's answer matching and random fallback and the prompts in Supplementary Section 9.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 982 compiled videos and 1,706 questions spanning five categories and 15 tasks. No datasets, domains, or test scenarios are added or removed.

E2.justification: Table 2 retains identical model, human, and random-baseline rows. Comparator membership also remains identical within the diagnostic comparisons in Tables 3–9 and the qualitative examples.

E3.justification: The accuracy metrics, prompting, default model hyperparameters, and evaluated configurations remain unchanged. The frame counts, encoder resolutions, decoder sizes, and training-data volumes reported in the main and supplementary analyses are identical.

E4.justification: Both versions contain the same analyses of input frames, encoder resolution, decoder size, and training-data volume, together with the same qualitative errors and answer-distribution analyses in the supplement.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting is identical across the tables and figures. Neither version adds repeated-run or seed information, uncertainty intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: All numerical entries and plotted or qualitative findings are unchanged, including supplementary results. For example, Table 2 reports human overall accuracy of 86.26 and LLaVA-OneVision-72B accuracy of 63.31 in both versions.

T1.justification: The formal prediction rule in Algorithm 1 and accuracy definitions in Equations 1–2 are identical. No mathematical assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs are added or removed.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain identical claims about the benchmark, the human–model performance gap, and the diagnostic contributions.

C2.justification: Interpretations and qualifications remain identical, including the proposed explanation involving redundant frames, the confounding of encoder resolution with model identity, and discussion of narrative and counting difficulties.

D1.justification: Dataset processing, annotation procedures, prompts, evaluation details, and the leaderboard/evaluation-code link are unchanged. The supplement adds no implementation or reproducibility information relative to v4.

R1.justification: The cited works, reference list, benchmark comparisons, and research positioning in the introduction and Section 5 are identical.

P1.justification: The marginal arXiv stamp changes from v4, 8 Oct 2025, to v5, 25 Nov 2025, and PDF author metadata is revised. The displayed author list, manuscript wording, and section structure remain identical.

P2.justification: Figures 1–14, Tables 1–9, captions, and page layout are unchanged. Rendered pages match exactly apart from the first-page version/date stamp; no displays are added, removed, redrawn, or relocated.

improvement.justification: The main paper and supplement retain identical scientific content, results, explanations, and presentation. The administrative version/date and metadata updates do not meaningfully affect clarity, evidential support, reproducibility, or overall paper quality.
